Params: The whale calls sound again, but they're faint today, as if carried from another world.
Afternoon light sifts through the leaves above. Blue rippled glass shimmers like water. There are also cotton candy, a banana split, and the bright cluster of balloons in a clown's hand.
The world sways gently, a warm voice singing without end. Karenina stays curled inside the dream.
She sees it now. The girl who holds her has bright, blazing hair... a vivid orange-red.
Red, as warm as fire. Red, as gentle as a mother's kiss. Red, as endless as the stream of blood that never stops flowing.
Is it red hair she sees? Or the blood-red dark of an endless night?
They're flying all the way to the heart of the sea.
The dream melts into a heavy, lightless dark. In the last moment before it all disappears, her grandfather's weary eyes look back at her.
The whale calls are right beside her now, sharp and cold as an Atlantic gale scraping past her ear.
Karenina's eyes snap wide. The tears come on their own, rolling down her cheeks, while her face remains hollow and expressionless as a marionette.
The sorrow that raged through the dream is wrenched out of her, and her frame goes rigid, cold as sculpted marble. Deep within, a chasm turns and turns, drinking down all feeling, all awareness.
The little potted plant picks up on the wrongness at once. It trundles off the nightstand and rolls across the mattress, pressing its glass biosphere gently against Karenina's tear-wet cheek.
The girl turns her head slowly, as if she cannot understand the little thing's distress. Her empty gaze drifts past everything and finds no place to land.
Rarana tumbles off the bed and scrabbles up the door on all four claws.
At that same moment, a frantic pounding shakes the door.
It scuttles sideways to the door panel like a tiny crab, its little claws clicking rapidly over the keypad. The biometric scanner would never recognize a biosphere, after all.
Just as you brace to shoulder the door open, it swings wide from the inside.
Those golden eyes blink, and life seeps back into them, little by little.
Commandant...? What are you doing here?
Oh... right. Someone took the room next door. All on their own.
Not that I asked you to... just so we're clear.
She seems drained, yet her mouth twitches with a tiny, self-pleased grin.
It was your worry over Karenina's unstable frame that made you switch your quarters next to hers the moment you came aboard the cable layer.
Rarana presses gently against the girl's cheek. It seems the little one has worked its quiet magic again.
But your frame sync rate dropped below safe levels.
Karenina checks her frame's readings, and the sync rate is gradually settling back within normal parameters.
Weariness pulls her eyes shut. The sea has given her nothing but puzzles, and they cling to her thoughts like relentless, tangled seaweed.
For tonight, at least, you hope she can have a peaceful sleep.
She turns onto her side, pressing one cheek into the soft bedding. Her pale golden eyes look out from the pillow, and a hand stretches forward, the fingers opening slightly.
A garden... grass, a glass table like water ripples, ice cream... and balloons.
Commandant, I'm thinking... where did I come from? I mean, before the slums, before everything.
I... never really asked that before.
Slum kids don't ask those things. It just makes people sad.
Grandpa didn't know either... And there was no one left to ask anyway...
Wherever you came from, you're Karenina now.
She wraps the blanket more snugly around her body.
(The person holding me in that dream... was that my mother?)
(The ocean... is that where I'm from...?)
I'm Karenina now. That's what matters.
Sleep pulls her under, deep and still.
The little potted plant scurries across from the pillow, its screen lighting up with that expression you know well.
When we're not feeling well, we tend to be gentler.
Not weak. She just became gentler.
You choose to hold your silence.
The little potted plant stretches out a small mechanical claw.
You extend one finger and touch it softly to Rarana's little claw.
A brief flicker runs across the little potted plant's virtual screen.
You extend one finger and touch it softly to Rarana's little claw.
A brief flicker runs across the little potted plant's virtual screen.
Night ebbs away, inch by inch. The cable layer pushes south alone through the dark sea.
Beneath the waves, the noise of rending meat and cracking bone is swallowed into silence. They are inside Fenrir's waters now.
Sava stares into the darkness over the ocean, an unease prickling beneath his skin.
Hear what? It's just waves. Relax, we're almost at Fenrir. Should be any minute now.
He squints into the distance. Soon, he finds the crimson swells that churn ahead, hidden by the early morning glow.
Wait! Red Tide... That's the Red Tide! Sound the alarm!
The morning shatters under the scream of alarms, and the rapid beat of boots echoes through every corridor.

The sea has been nearly consumed by the Red Tide. Gray-blue surrenders to deep red, and the red curdles into a thick, brownish crimson that heaves with the swell as if it were a living membrane, the hide of some breathing leviathan.

Fenrir is ringed by the Red Tide. It was once the home of the southern central AI, the choke point of the Atlantic fiber-optic network. Now the dark red waters circle it like fingers around a giant's throat, each wave a labored gasp.
Karenina hurries to the bow, her hair still messy and uncombed, and falls in beside you.
The cable ship can't go any further. Without the Balder's anti-Punishing Virus shielding, we'd get swallowed the second we crossed over...
Then... what about the protocol and the repeaters?
I can handle that on my own.
My surfboard can make the crossing. I'll take the provisional protocol over first and override the old one.
Keep the captain's seat warm for me.
